title: KV-cache-and-adapter-samplecode-workshop-walkthrough
content:
Objective:
This hands-on walkthrough prepares participants to build a lightweight inference adapter that sits in front of Redwood-hosted or private model endpoints and adds prefix/KV caching and adaptive batching. Goal is a repeatable mini-POC that demonstrates a ~2x cost reduction for high-prefix reuse workloads while keeping p95 latency under SLO.

Audience and duration:
- Audience: Solutions engineers, customer ML/infra engineers, and platform engineers who will own private deployments or integrations.
- Duration: 2.5 hours (self-paced sections + 60 minute guided debugging lab).

Prereqs (local laptop + cluster):
- Git + Docker installed.
- kubectl configured to a dev k8s cluster (minikube / KIND / EKS dev cluster).
- Access token for a Redwood test model endpoint (env var REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- Python 3.10, venv recommended.
- Redis (or in-cluster equivalent) available for prefix/KV cache (we provide a manifest).

High-level approach (what we ship in the lab):
1) A small FastAPI adapter that accepts chat/generation requests, computes a deterministic prefix key (hash of prompt template + last N tokens), and checks a Redis-backed KV cache.
2) If cache hit -> return cached completion with a header noting cache-age; if miss -> forward to Redwood endpoint with batching disabled for single-request correctness, then write back into cache.
3) An autoscaling k8s deployment with a simple sidecar prometheus exporter and an init container that warms the local cache with popular prefixes.
4) A canary routing example: how to split by header and fallback to a cheaper float-quantized model when throughput is saturated.

Lab steps (est. times):
- Setup and inspection (20m)
- Run adapter locally + smoke tests (30m)
- Deploy to cluster + observe metrics (30m)
- Simulate traffic and tune cache TTL + batching (40m)
- Guided debugging and failure scenarios (30m)

Key files in the repo (what we use in the walkthrough):
- adapter/main.py  -- FastAPI adapter and batching logic
- adapter/cache.py -- Redis helpers and prefix hashing utilities
- k8s/deploy.yaml  -- Deployment + Service + HPA + initJob
- k8s/redis.yaml   -- Lightweight Redis instance for dev
- scripts/loadtest.py -- simple async load generator to exercise prefix reuse
- examples/prometheus-metrics.md -- what to scrape and dashboards to expect

Quickstart (local run)
1) clone + venv
   git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/adapter-examples.git
   cd adapter-examples/kv-cache-adapter
   python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
   pip install -r requirements.txt

2) set envs and run
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
   export REDWOOD_ENDPOINT=https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
   export REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0
   python -m adapter.main --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

3) smoke test (curl)
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"Summarize: The quick brown fox...","max_tokens":80}' | jq .

Core snippet: deterministic prefix hashing (adapter/cache.py) (note: formatting here is intentionally compact for the doc)

   def prefix_key(prompt_template: str, history_tokens: List[str], window: int = 64) -> str:
       # use stable tokenization + sha256; key includes template id to avoid cross-prompt collisions
       recent = " ".join(history_tokens[-window:])
       key_material = f"{prompt_template}|{recent}"
       return "pref:" + hashlib.sha256(key_material.encode()).hexdigest()

Batching policy (simple adaptive):
- Adapter buffers incoming requests up to batch_max_size (default: 8) or batch_timeout_ms (default: 20ms).
- If a request has a high-probability cache hit (prefix seen in last N minutes) we flush immediately to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Export batch size distribution metric to tune kernel-friendly batch sizes (we want most batches at 2,4,8 depending on model).

Kubernetes notes (k8s/deploy.yaml highlights):
- Use requests/limits: cpu: 500m, memory: 1024Mi for adapter containers; set ephemeral-storage and a small local prom exporter.
- InitJob to prefetch 500 top prefixes into Redis on start (script pulls list from configmap/popular-prefixes.txt).
- HPA based on custom metric adapter_cache_miss_rate: if miss rate > 0.6 and p95 latency > 800ms, scale +1 replica.

Observability (what to look for)
- Metrics exposed by adapter: adapter_requests_total, adapter_batch_size_histogram, adapter_cache_hit_ratio, adapter_forward_latency_ms, adapter_cache_write_latency_ms.
- Dashboards: show p50/p95 forward latency (no-cache vs cached), cache hit rate over time, token/sec served per replica.
- Distributed traces: add a Redwood span-id header when forwarding so Redwood Console traces show end-to-end.

Testing and tuning exercises (guided)
1) High prefix reuse scenario: run scripts/loadtest.py with --pattern common to simulate reuse. Expected: cache_hit_ratio > 0.65, overall token cost reduces ~50% on synthetic workload.
2) Low reuse scenario: run with random prompts. Expected: cache_miss spikes; observe batching behavior and increase batch_max_size to improve throughput.
3) Canary scenario: deploy a second adapter variant that uses a quantized model endpoint and route 10% traffic by header X-Canary. Observe quality delta in sampled completions.

Known failure modes + how to debug quickly
- Stale cache leading to hallucinated repeated completions: increase prefix granularity (include role markers + last-turn hash) and shorten TTL.
- Redis eviction causing high miss rate under load: switch to larger instance or configure LRU eviction policy and use a tiered cache (local LRU + Redis).
- Head-of-line blocking when a large request enters the batch: detect oversized requests (tokens > threshold) and bypass batching path.

Workshop discussion prompts (for customers):
- Where in your traffic do you see prefix reuse? (examples: email thread replies, template-based replies, code completions)
- What are acceptable freshness windows for cached completions?
- Are there regulatory constraints on caching user-provided content? If so, how to implement per-tenant TTLs and purge?

Appendix: small sample Kubernetes manifest excerpt
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: kv-adapter
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kv-adapter
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: kv-adapter
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: adapter
        image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/kv-adapter:latest
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "1024Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "1000m"
            memory: "2Gi"
        env:
        - name: REDWOOD_API_KEY
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: redwood-creds
              key: api_key
        - name: REDIS_URL
          value: redis://redis:6379/0

Appendix: quick checklist for delivery to customers
- Confirm prefix reuse patterns on a 1-week sample of production logs.
- Agree cache TTLs and privacy policy for cached content.
- Run a 24–72 hour canary with traffic split 95/5 and sampling for quality evaluation.
- Add cost tracking in Redwood Console: token units by route/model before/after adapter.

References and further reading:
- internal: RD-4312 notes (linked)
- GitHub: example adapter repo (linked)
- Confluence: KV Cache playbook (linked)

Notes to facilitator (brief):
- Emphasize experimentation: different workloads will favor different batching vs caching ratios.
- Keep an eye on cache-hit skew by tenant — a small number of tenants may account for most savings; discuss per-tenant controls.
- For private deployments, advise customers to run Redis in a managed mode or replace with a local LRU for very low-latency needs.

END OF WALKTHROUGH

Quick contact: priya.shah@redwood.ai (owner) for follow-ups and repo access requests.
